1. Title: Suboptimal DOM Manipulation (innerHTML with escaping)
   Category: Code Quality
   Severity: Low
   Confidence: High
   File: N/A
   Line: 10
   Evidence: `el.innerHTML = escapeHtml(req.query.name);`
   Data Flow: `req.query.name` (External Source) → `escapeHtml` (Sanitizer) → `el.innerHTML` (HTML Sink)
   Why It Matters: While the use of `escapeHtml` prevents XSS (security), setting `innerHTML` is generally discouraged for user data due to performance overhead and the risk that an escape function might miss a character or be bypassed in edge cases. Using `textContent` is the robust, performant standard.
   Why It Was Detected: The code uses a visible sanitizer (`escapeHtml`) to reach an HTML sink (`innerHTML`), triggering the "sanitized sink" rule which flags it for code quality/performance review rather than vulnerability.
   Recommended Fix: Use `textContent` or `createTextNode` to set the text content directly, avoiding the need for escaping.
   Manual Verification Required: No
   Why this is not necessarily a vulnerability: The `escapeHtml` function effectively neutralizes the XSS risk. The finding is purely about code robustness and performance.
   Vulnerable Code: `el.innerHTML = escapeHtml(req.query.name);`
   Fixed Code: `el.textContent = req.query.name;`

2. Title: Inline Event Handler in Response
   Category: Code Quality
   Severity: Low
   Confidence: High
   File: N/A
   Line: 28
   Evidence: `res.send('<button onclick="toggleMenu()">Menu</button>');`
   Data Flow: N/A
   Why It Matters: Inline event handlers (like `onclick`) are brittle and can be blocked by Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, making the application less robust and harder to maintain in production environments.
   Why It Was Detected: The code contains an inline event handler pattern, which is a best-practice violation (Code Quality/CSP hardening) unless it processes untrusted data (which it does not here).
   Recommended Fix: Use event listeners attached in JavaScript or server-side rendering frameworks that support secure attribute binding.
   Manual Verification Required: No
   Why this is not necessarily a vulnerability: There is no user input being processed by the `toggleMenu` function, so there is no security risk.
   Vulnerable Code: `res.send('<button onclick="toggleMenu()">Menu</button>');`
   Fixed Code: `res.send('<button id="menuBtn">Menu</button>');` (followed by `document.getElementById('menuBtn').addEventListener('click', toggleMenu);` in client-side JS)
